products.name: Meridian
products.summary: Built for the depths, finished for the boardroom — a dive watch that has never once been near the sea.
description: The Meridian takes its architecture from the tool watches of the 1960s: a unidirectional bezel, luminous markers, and a case built to survive far more than it will ever be asked to.
Every Meridian is regulated to within two seconds a day before it leaves the workshop — a tolerance we consider the minimum, not the achievement.

products.name: Regent
products.summary: A watch that disappears under a cuff and reappears the moment it matters.
description: The Regent is deliberately quiet: a slim case, a single hand-finished dial, no complication that doesn't earn its place.
It is built for evenings, not expeditions — the kind of restraint that only becomes obvious once you've worn it.

products.name: Calibre
products.summary: The watch we would keep if we could only ever make one.
description: Calibre carries our in-house movement, assembled and adjusted by a single watchmaker from first part to final seal.
Its design has changed only twice in three decades — proof, we think, that some ideas don't need improving.

products.name: Apex
products.summary: An architectural case for a movement built to be seen, not just told about.
description: The Apex pairs an openworked dial with an angular, faceted case — every surface catches light differently as your wrist moves.
It's the boldest piece in the collection, built for the days you don't want your watch to whisper.

products.name: Velocity
products.summary: Less a watch than a piece of machinery you happen to wear.
description: Velocity strips the case back to a single question: how little can hold a movement together and still feel indestructible?
The answer is a tonneau-shaped shell in carbon composite, light enough to forget and stiff enough to trust.
